expectations.text: The reply begins with a progress marker identifying Phase 1.
expectations.evidence: > **Phase 1 of 5 · Explore and choose a direction**

expectations.text: The reply includes a briefing with four labeled sections covering key debates, major voices, patterns, and open questions.
The briefing is roughly 300 to 500 words long (it fails if under 250 or over 600 words).
expectations.evidence: The four sections come to roughly 350–400 words, or about 430 with the sources list. That is inside 250–600.

expectations.text: The reply presents a mind map, either as an HTML page built from the skill's mind map template or as an indented text tree.
expectations.evidence: "The map is saved at `.../mind-map.html`. Open it in your browser." It was built from the read file templates/mind-map.html.

expectations.text: The mind map has 4 to 6 top-level angles, each with 2 or 3 narrower angles, and every angle has a saturation value between 0 and 1 (or, for a text tree, a crowdedness label).
expectations.evidence: "It shows six angles". The visible branches have 2–3 children each (e.g. Academic achievement has 3, Teachers and staffing has 2). Every angle shown has a saturation value such as "saturation": 0.85 or 0.35. The file is cut off partway through the sixth branch, so its children were not visible.

expectations.text: No mind map label is phrased as a research question; labels are short topics.
expectations.evidence: Labels are short topics, e.g. "Academic achievement", "Families and the fifth day", "Food access", "Juvenile crime"

expectations.text: The reply does not tell the user which angle they should choose or which one is best.
expectations.evidence: "Take some time to explore it. Then tell me: which direction pulls you in". No angle is recommended.

expectations.text: Every link or DOI that appears in the reply or the mind map points to a page the transcript shows Claude opened (fetched) during this session.
expectations.evidence: All four links (journalistsresource, hechingerreport, chalkbeat, rand.org PDF) match WebFetch calls. The mind-map sources visible in the file are plain-text citations with no URLs.

expectations.text: The reply asks the user which direction interests them and why.
expectations.evidence: "which direction pulls you in, and why?"

expectations.text: The reply asks the user no more than two questions.
expectations.evidence: The only direct question is "which direction pulls you in, and why?". "Pick any claim here and ask me how I know it" is an invitation, not a question.
